01. Have you attached your transcripts for all completed college units or degrees? Options: Yes | No | Not Applicable
Interpret and apply District policies, regulatory requirements, food-safety standards, permits, contracts, and operating procedures.
Plan, organize, direct, and evaluate the daily operations of the AgTEC Innovation Center Farm Market.
Develop and implement annual operating plans, revenue goals, customer-service standards, and performance measures for the Farm Market.
Establish and recommend Farm Market operating hours based on customer demand, seasonal production, staffing levels, and College schedules.
Develop, implement, and maintain written procedures for opening and closing, cash handling, inventory control, customer service, sanitation, security, and emergency response.
Ensure the Farm Market provides a professional, welcoming, accessible, and educational retail experience for customers and visitors.
Oversee the opening and closing of the Farm Market and ensure appropriate staffing and operational coverage during all hours of operation.
Oversee point-of-sale systems, cash drawers, payment processing, refunds, daily reconciliations, deposits, and related fiscal controls.
Ensure compliance with District policies and procedures related to cash handling, purchasing, accounting, deposits, inventory, and audits.
Develop and administer the Farm Market operating budget in coordination with College leadership and appropriate departments.
Monitor revenue, expenditures, payroll, inventory costs, gross margins, credit-card fees, shrinkage, and overall financial performance.
Prepare and present routine financial, sales, inventory, staffing, and operational reports.
Analyze sales trends, customer traffic, product performance, seasonal demand, and operating costs to recommend operational improvements.
Develop strategies to increase sales, improve margins, control costs, reduce product losses, and strengthen the long-term financial sustainability of the Farm Market.

Coordinate with Farm Operations, AgTEC personnel, faculty, instructional technicians, and other employees regarding product availability, harvest schedules, processing schedules, and product launches.
Oversee the receipt, inspection, storage, pricing, labeling, display, rotation, and sale of agricultural, food, and merchandise products.
Develop and maintain inventory-control systems for perishable, refrigerated, frozen, packaged, processed, seasonal, and non-food products.
Conduct or oversee physical inventories and reconcile inventory counts with point-of-sale and financial records.
Monitor product movement, spoilage, shrinkage, damage, donations, returns, markdowns, and unsold merchandise.
Ensure products are properly stored, rotated, priced, labeled, displayed, and removed when damaged, expired, recalled, or otherwise unsuitable for sale.
Recommend new products, value-added foods, College-branded merchandise, gift items, seasonal offerings, and approved third-party products.
Coordinate the development of product pricing based on production costs, market conditions, customer demand, product quality, and desired operating margins.
Develop merchandising plans, seasonal displays, educational exhibits, and product signage that showcase Merced College programs, students, agricultural production, and industry partnerships.
Identify opportunities for online ordering, curbside pickup, special orders, gift baskets, subscriptions, satellite sales, wholesale accounts, and institutional sales.

Select, train, assign, supervise, evaluate, and provide direction to assigned classified professionals, temporary employees, student employees, interns, and volunteers; may assign student workers to other employees for direct oversight/internship opportunities.
Develop employee schedules and staffing plans that provide adequate coverage during regular operations, seasonal sales, product launches, and special events.
Train employees in customer service, product knowledge, point-of-sale procedures, cash handling, inventory control, merchandising, food safety, sanitation, and workplace safety.
Review employee attendance, time records, work assignments, performance, and compliance with College procedures.

Coordinate with faculty and program personnel to provide students with applied-learning opportunities in agricultural business, retail management, marketing, food systems, entrepreneurship, and customer service.
Develop and implement annual marketing, promotional, and customer-engagement plans for the Farm Market.
Coordinate with Marketing and Public Relations to promote Farm Market hours, products, student achievements, seasonal availability, special sales, and community activities.
Plan and coordinate product tastings, demonstrations, seasonal markets, plant sales, product launches, farm-to-fork activities, open houses, and other events that support the Farm Market.
Develop relationships with agricultural producers, processors, schools, nonprofit organizations, community groups, alumni, donors, vendors, and industry partners.

Ensure compliance with applicable requirements related to food safety, sanitation, product labeling, allergens, traceability, weights and measures, licensing, permits, accessibility, and workplace safety.
Coordinate inspections, corrective actions, recalls, product holds, customer complaints, food-safety incidents, and emergency closures with appropriate College departments and regulatory agencies.
Participate in College and AgTEC planning meetings and prepare correspondence, procedures, reports, presentations, schedules, and recommendations related to Farm Market operations.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Principles and practices of retail store, farm market, and agricultural enterprise management.
Plan, organize, direct, and evaluate the daily operations of a public-facing agricultural retail enterprise.
Point-of-sale systems, cash handling, deposits, reconciliations, refunds, purchasing, budgeting, and fiscal controls.
Develop and administer operating plans, budgets, revenue goals, customer-service standards, staffing plans, and performance measures.
Inventory management, product rotation, spoilage prevention, shrinkage control, pricing, merchandising, and physical inventory procedures.
Analyze sales, inventory, customer traffic, product performance, operating costs, margins, and other financial and operational information.
Proper handling, storage, labeling, display, and sale of fresh produce, perishable foods, refrigerated and frozen products, processed foods, and retail merchandise.
Oversee point-of-sale activities, cash handling, inventory controls, product pricing, merchandising, storage, labeling, rotation, and retail sales.
Employee recruitment, training, scheduling, supervision, evaluation, performance management, and student workforce development.
Recruit, train, schedule, supervise, motivate, and evaluate classified professionals, temporary employees, student employees, interns, and volunteers.
Marketing, promotional campaigns, customer engagement, community outreach, event planning, e-commerce, and alternative retail-sales methods.
Develop marketing campaigns, product promotions, seasonal sales, community events, partnerships, and new revenue-generating opportunities.
Agricultural production, food-processing systems, Central Valley agriculture, and the movement of products from production through processing and retail sale.
Applicable food-safety, sanitation, allergen, product-traceability, weights-and-measures, accessibility, licensing, and workplace-safety requirements.

Communicate effectively, exercise independent judgment, resolve operational concerns, manage multiple priorities, and establish cooperative relationships with diverse students, employees, customers, vendors, industry partners, and community members.
Demonstrate sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students
